title: EGA VI. Plans, notations, problèmes ouverts : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page proves that every point of the étale topos of a (pre)scheme X comes from a geometric point, via strict localization. The point is given as a fibre functor φ: X̃_ét → Ens that commutes with colimits and finite limits.

(1) Restrict φ to the subobjects of the final object of X̃_ét. These are the opens of the topos, which by 6.1 are the same as the Zariski opens U ⊂ X. Since φ preserves finite limits, φ(U) ⊂ φ(e) = pt, so φ(U) is empty or a single point. This gives a map φ0: U(X) → {0,1} that commutes with arbitrary sups and finite infs. In modern terms it is a frame map O(X) → Ω, i.e. a completely prime filter of opens, i.e. a point of the locale O(X).

(2) X is sober: every irreducible closed set has exactly one generic point. Hence φ0 is the indicator of the opens containing a unique point x ∈ X. Explicitly, the complement of the union of all U with φ0(U) = 0 is irreducible closed, and x is its generic point.

(3) For any sheaf F, its image in the final object is an open U, and F → U is an epimorphism. Since φ preserves epimorphisms, φ(F) ≠ ∅ iff x ∈ U.

(4) Form the category of elements C_φ of pairs (X', ξ) with X' étale over X and ξ ∈ φ(X'). By 7.9.1 its opposite is pseudo-filtrant and connected (cofiltered). Applying step (3) to X' instead of X, each (X', ξ) determines a unique x' ∈ X'. For an étale X'' → X', ξ lies in the image of φ(X'') → φ(X') iff x' lies in the image of X''.

(5) It follows that the projective limit of the X' over C_φ exists as a prescheme and is a strict localization Z of X. Z thus corresponds to a geometric point ξ̄ with fibre functor ε_ξ, which is then to be identified with φ.

This is exactly the proof that the points of X̃_ét are the geometric points up to equivalence (SGA 4 VIII 7.9). The cross-references 6.1, 7.9.1 and 7.9.2 match the numbering of SGA 4 Exposé VIII. The page, numbered (32, appears to be a typescript sheet of that exposé (or a draft of it), filed in the EGA VI folder. It carries a large pencil diagonal stroke, the usual mark of a superseded or discarded sheet.
errors: The prescheme limit over C_φ exists only after restricting to a cofinal subcategory of pairs (X', ξ) with X' affine (the transition maps must be affine). This is left implicit in 'on conclut de ceci'.
Typo in the original: '(X',ξ) ∈ Ob X_ét' should read '∈ Ob C_φ'.
Typo in the original: 'réduit un point' should read 'réduit à un point'.
The final identification of φ with ε_ξ (an isomorphism of fibre functors) is not carried out on this page.

ideas.what: Opens of the étale topos correspond to Zariski opens. A point of the topos induces a frame map O(X) → {0,1}, and sobriety of X yields a unique point x.
ideas.modern_name: Points of a locale / completely prime filters; sober spaces

ideas.what: Every point of X̃_ét is isomorphic to the fibre functor at a geometric point, obtained as the limit over the category of elements, which is a strict localization.
ideas.modern_name: Points of the étale topos = geometric points (strict henselizations)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. VIII, Théorème 7.9 and Prop. 7.9.1–7.9.2

ideas.what: The category of elements of a point (fibre functor) is cofiltered and connected.
ideas.modern_name: Flat functors / category of elements of a point

deep.surprise_reason: This is a crossed-out typescript page of the standard proof in SGA 4 VIII 7.9 (points of the étale topos are geometric points), with matching numbering. Its only interest is archival: it was misfiled among the EGA VI plans. It contains no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'réduit un point' is as typed in the original; the intended text is 'réduit à un point'.
'x E U' in the displayed condition should be read as 'x ∈ U'.
'C_φ°' is the opposite category, written with a superscript °.
The struck-out words in 'les préschémas' should be read 'le préschéma' (s's overstruck), followed by the underlined lim with a left arrow (projective limit).
The whole page is crossed by a long pencil diagonal stroke, indicating it was cancelled. The transcription does not record this.
The blue-ink scribbled word after 'On voit facilement' is illegible, deleted text.
